faq: How do you decide the attribute values?
We build a short list of allowed values with you first, for example a fixed set of colors and materials. This keeps filters tidy instead of creating hundreds of near duplicates.
Can it read details from product photos?
Yes for obvious features such as color or style. For details a photo cannot show, such as fabric content, we rely on your text and mark gaps for you to fill.
Will you change my existing product data?
Only fields that are empty, unless you ask us to standardize others. We keep a before and after sheet so any change can be reversed.
Do you work with Shopify metafields?
Yes. We can fill standard fields and metafields, and set up filters in themes that support them. Tell us the platform and theme in the order form.

desc:
Product catalog enrichment fills the blank attributes, tags and categories in your store so shoppers can filter and find items. Ecom Swift LLC reads each product's title, description and images, then returns a clean sheet or loads the values straight into your store.

## What is product catalog enrichment?

Product catalog enrichment is the work of adding the missing data that sits behind each product: color, size, material, style, category and tags. The data is often absent because products were imported from a supplier file, added in a hurry, or entered by several people with different habits. The text on the page may describe a navy cotton shirt, while the color and material fields stay empty.

Those empty fields matter because stores, search tools and shopping feeds all read structured values, not sentences. A product with no color value cannot appear when someone filters by navy. Enrichment turns what is already written and photographed into values the store can actually use.

## Why complete attributes change how shoppers behave

Shoppers on a large catalog rarely scroll every page. They narrow the list with filters, then compare what is left. If half the products carry no color or material value, those products vanish from the filtered view, and the shopper never learns they exist.

Consistent categories help in the same way. When similar products sit under different names, such as "tee", "t-shirt" and "tshirts", collections split apart and navigation feels untidy. Clean values make collections accurate, make on-site search more relevant and give Google Shopping feeds and marketplace listings the fields they ask for. The outcome still depends on your range, prices and traffic, but missing data is one of the few causes of lost sales that you can fully remove.

## What a well enriched catalog includes

- One agreed list of allowed values for every attribute, so "navy" never appears as "dark blue" on another product.
- Color, size, material, style, fit and use case filled where the product supports them.
- Categories and collection suggestions that match how shoppers search, not how a supplier files its stock.
- Tags merged and tidied, with duplicates, typos and near matches combined.
- Values read from the title, description and product images, and cross-checked against each other.
- A clear mark on products where the evidence is thin or conflicting, so a person decides.
- Variants handled correctly, with option names and values consistent across products.
- Existing good data left untouched unless you ask us to replace it.
- A sheet showing the old value, the new value and the reason for each change.
- Storefront filters that actually use the new fields.

## How we do the work

We start with an export of your catalog and a short call or message about how your customers shop. From that we draft the attribute list and allowed values, and send them for your approval before anything is filled in.

Next we process the products. Each item is read for evidence in its title, description and photos, and values are chosen only from your approved list. Where two sources disagree, or an image is unclear, we mark the product for review rather than guess.

Delivery depends on the package. The Basic package returns a reviewed sheet for a first set of products. The Standard package loads the values back into your store and merges duplicate tags. The Premium package covers a full catalog, sets up storefront filters, has a person check a sample by hand and leaves you a naming sheet so new products follow the same rules. If you use Shopify, we can also fill product metafields that your theme reads for filters.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Approve the value list before bulk changes begin.
- Keep attribute names short and plain, the way shoppers say them.
- Decide which fields are required for every new product.
- Review the marked items, because you know your range best.
- Keep a copy of the original export in case you want to compare.

**Avoid:**
- Inventing a new tag for every product, which recreates the mess.
- Mixing units, such as inches and centimeters, in one field.
- Filling a field when the product gives no evidence for it.
- Adding more attributes than your filters will ever display.
- Overwriting good existing data just to make the sheet look uniform.

## Who this service is for

It suits a store owner who imported a supplier catalog and now has thousands of half-filled products. It suits a seller moving from a marketplace into their own store, where listings used different fields. It also suits a growing brand whose staff have tagged products in different ways over several seasons, and who now want filters and collections that behave.

## What we need from you

Send a product export from your store, plus any supplier sheets that hold extra detail. Tell us the attributes shoppers ask about most and share three or four sample products you consider well described. We never need your password: if we load data back into your store, you give us collaborator, staff or developer access with limited permissions. We reply after your order with a short checklist and keep you informed until the final sheet is approved.
